mainTopic: רבי יצחק's teaching about a זב and רב הונא; the unimmersed יולדת; and the dispute between רב and לוי over one source of blood or two.
overview: The amud opens by finishing רבי יצחק's teaching: the separate section on a זב makes him easier in one way (he is not made impure through אונס) and stricter in another (he makes משכב ומושב impure). The גמרא first reads this as being about the first sighting, which would contradict רב הונא. It then rereads it as being about the second sighting, so רב הונא's rule stands. רב הונא also describes how זוב looks different from שכבת זרע. Next the גמרא turns to the משנה about a יולדת who did not immerse. A ברייתא shows בית הלל and בית שמאי trading proofs, and the גמרא settles which case they argue about: a יולדת בזוב who counted her clean days. Then רב (one source of blood) and לוי (two sources that take turns) argue about the blood after childbirth, and they rule differently when the flow keeps going past a boundary day. The גמרא tests both views against the משנה and finds a way to explain it under each one. It finally brings a ברייתא on דותה תטמא that fits רב, and the challenge against לוי continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of רבי יצחק's teaching: the זב's stringency
steps.stepSummary: The quote of רבי יצחק ends with the stringency: a זב makes his bedding and seat impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: …that he makes bedding and seats impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting רבי יצחק's statement. This is the last piece of the source it is about to analyze.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק said the זב was given his own section in the תורה for two reasons. One is a leniency: he is not made impure through אונס. The other is a stringency: he makes משכב ומושב impure, which a בעל קרי does not.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who has an unusual discharge, which makes him ritually impure
Something he lies on, which becomes impure
Something he sits on, which becomes impure

phrases.english: that he makes bedding and seats impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quote of רבי יצחק that was begun before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זב makes משכב ומושב impure, which a בעל קרי does not.

steps.title: רבי יצחק must mean the first sighting, contradicting רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that רבי יצחק must be talking about the first sighting. That would mean a first sighting through אונס is not impure, against רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is he talking about? If you say the second sighting, how was he ever included under בעל קרי at that stage? So it must be the first sighting. Yet רבי יצחק teaches that the leniency is that he is not made impure through אונס!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which sighting רבי יצחק means, and decides it must be the first one. That turns his words into a challenge against רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After a second sighting the man is already a full זב, so he was never 'included' with a בעל קרי at that point. So רבי יצחק seems to mean the first sighting. But then he says a first sighting through אונס is not impure, while רב הונא says it is.

keyTerms.meaning: The first time he sees a discharge
The second time he sees a discharge
A man who had a seminal emission
Something caused by outside circumstances, beyond his control
If you say (suggesting one option, usually to reject it)

phrases.english: When? If we say at the second sighting —
where was he ever included in the category of one with a seminal emission?
Rather, it is obvious he means the first sighting,
and yet he teaches 'to be lenient with him':
that he is not made impure through a discharge beyond his control!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי יצחק's statement as a challenge against רב הונא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that a זב's first sighting is impure even through אונס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יצחק's leniency must refer to the first sighting, since the second sighting was never grouped with בעל קרי. So a first sighting through אונס would not be impure.

steps.title: The stringency cannot be about the first sighting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: רבי יצחק's stringency of משכב ומושב cannot apply at a first sighting, so he cannot be talking about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think so? He also says 'to be stringent with him, that he makes bedding and seats impure.' Is a man after his first sighting able to make bedding and seats impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea that רבי יצחק is talking about the first sighting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man with only one sighting is like a בעל קרי and does not make משכב ומושב impure. Since רבי יצחק's stringency does not fit the first sighting, the reading behind the challenge falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: And can you really think so? (used to reject an assumption)
To be strict with him
Fit for, able to

phrases.english: And can you really think so? 'To be stringent with him':
that he makes bedding and seats impure —

phrases.aramaic: בִּרְאִיָּיה רִאשׁוֹנָה בַּר מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב הוּא?
phrases.english: at the first sighting, is he able to make bedding and seats impure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the assumption in step 2 that רבי יצחק is talking about the first sighting.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading of רבי יצחק as being about the first sighting
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The stringency of משכב ומושב does not apply at a first sighting, so the two halves of רבי יצחק's statement cannot both be about it.

steps.title: Rereading רבי יצחק as talking about the second sighting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains what רבי יצחק really meant. At his first sighting the זב is grouped with a בעל קרי, but at his second sighting he gets his own rules: a leniency and a stringency.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what רבי יצחק means: Wasn't a זב included under בעל קרי at his first sighting? So why was he taken out at his second sighting? To be lenient with him and to be strict with him. Lenient: he is not made impure through אונס. Strict: he makes bedding and seats impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rereads רבי יצחק so that both his leniency and his stringency are about the second sighting. That removes the contradiction with רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first sighting stays in the בעל קרי group, so it can be impure even through אונס, just as רב הונא said. Only the second sighting gets the special rules: it does not count if it came through אונס, and it makes משכב ומושב impure.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means (a rereading of a statement)
Was taken out (separated from a general category)
To be lenient with him

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יצחק's leniency (not impure through אונס) and stringency (משכב ומושב) both apply only to the second sighting. The first sighting is still like a בעל קרי, so רב הונא's rule stands.
steps.confusionAlert: The 'leniency' is not that a זב is less impure than a בעל קרי overall. It only means a second sighting caused by אונס does not count toward making him a זב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves רב הונא's rule that a זב's first sighting is impure even through אונס.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הָכִי קָאָמַר, רַבִּי יִצְחָק אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rather, this is what he is saying — Rabbi Yitzchak says:

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲלֹא זָב בִּכְלַל בַּעַל קֶרִי הָיָה
phrases.english: But wasn't a זב included in the category of one with a seminal emission

phrases.aramaic: בִּרְאִיָּיה רִאשׁוֹנָה, וְלָמָּה יָצָא בִּרְאִיָּיה שְׁנִיָּיה —
phrases.english: at the first sighting? So why was he taken out at the second sighting?
To be lenient with him and to be strict with him.
To be lenient with him: he is not made impure through a discharge beyond his control;

phrases.aramaic: וּלְהַחְמִיר עָלָיו — שֶׁהוּא עוֹשֶׂה מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב.
phrases.english: and to be strict with him: he makes bedding and seats impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָכִי קָאָמַר, רַבִּי יִצְחָק אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the rejection in step 3 and offers the correct reading of רבי יצחק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יצחק's leniency about אונס applies to the first sighting, against רב הונא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both the leniency and the stringency apply to the second sighting only, so רב הונא's rule about the first sighting stands.

steps.title: How זוב looks compared to שכבת זרע
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא describes זוב and contrasts it with שכבת זרע in three ways: what it looks like, where it comes from, and how thick it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: זוב looks like the water of barley dough. זוב comes from 'dead flesh,' while שכבת זרע comes from 'living flesh.' זוב is runny and looks like the white of an egg that cannot hatch. שכבת זרע is thick and looks like the white of an egg that can hatch.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב הונא's description of what זוב actually looks like, so we can tell it apart from שכבת זרע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our discussion of a זב has been about when a discharge counts as זוב. רב הונא gives practical signs to tell the two discharges apart. זוב is thin, watery, and comes without arousal. שכבת זרע is thick, sticky, and comes with arousal.

keyTerms.meaning: An unusual discharge that makes a man a זב
Semen
Runny, watery
Thick, sticky (literally 'tied together')
An egg that cannot hatch into a chick

steps.whatToRemember: זוב is thin, watery, and comes without arousal. שכבת זרע is thick and comes with arousal. This closes the discussion of a זב.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: זוֹב דּוֹמֶה לְמֵי בָצֵק שֶׁל שְׂעוֹרִים.
phrases.english: Ziva is similar to the water of barley dough.
Ziva comes from dead flesh,
phrases.notes: He means the body is not aroused when זוב comes out.

phrases.english: semen comes from living flesh.
Ziva is runny,
and it is similar to the white of an egg that cannot hatch,
semen is thick,
and it is similar to the white of an egg that can hatch.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: זוֹב דּוֹמֶה לְמֵי בָצֵק שֶׁל שְׂעוֹרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion of a זב by describing what זוב physically looks like.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זוב is thin and watery and comes without arousal. שכבת זרע is thick and comes with arousal.

steps.title: New topic: blood of a woman who gave birth but did not immerse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, about a יולדת who did not yet immerse.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'The blood of a woman who gave birth and did not immerse, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, בית שמאי say this blood makes things impure only while it is wet. בית הלל say it is like the blood of a נדה and makes things impure whether wet or dry. The question is whether her not immersing keeps her in the full status of a נדה.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who gave birth
She immersed in a מקוה

phrases.english: The blood of a woman who gave birth and did not immerse, etc.
phrases.notes: 'Etc.' points to the rest of the משנה: בית שמאי say it makes things impure only when wet, and בית הלל say wet or dry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new section that moves on from the topic of a זב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute about whether a יולדת who did not immerse is treated as a full נדה for the purity status of her blood.

steps.title: בית הלל compare her to a נדה who did not immerse
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל argue that just as a נדה who did not immerse stays fully impure, so does a יולדת who did not immerse.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: בית הלל said to בית שמאי: Don't you agree that a נדה who did not immerse and then saw blood is impure?
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל try to prove their view by pointing to a case that בית שמאי already agree with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that a נדה stays a נדה until she immerses, even after her days have passed. בית הלל say a יולדת should be the same. Until she immerses, her blood should count as full נדה blood.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman impure because of her monthly period
You agree, you admit
Impure

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, אָמְרוּ לָהֶן בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי:
phrases.english: It is taught: Beit Hillel said to Beit Shammai:
Do you not agree regarding a menstruating woman

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא טָבְלָה וְרָאֲתָה דָּם, שֶׁהִיא טְמֵאָה?
phrases.english: who did not immerse and saw blood, that she is impure?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אַתֶּם מוֹדִים בְּנִדָּה שֶׁלֹּא טָבְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that spells out the argument behind the משנה's dispute.
steps.raayaObject: בית הלל's view that a יולדת who did not immerse has the full status of a נדה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The agreed rule that a נדה who did not immerse is still fully impure

steps.title: בית שמאי reject the comparison to a נדה
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי point out that a נדה is stricter than a יולדת, so we cannot learn from one to the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי said to them: No. You say this about a נדה, who is impure if she sees blood even after she immerses. Will you say it about a יולדת, who is pure if she immerses and then sees blood?
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי push back on בית הלל's proof. They show that the two cases are not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a נדה, immersion does not protect her from new blood, because any new blood makes her impure again. For a יולדת, after immersion she is in her days of purity, and new blood does not make her impure. Since her impurity is weaker, not immersing should not turn her into a full נדה.

keyTerms.meaning: If you said this about one case, will you say it about the other? (a formula for showing two cases are different)
Pure

phrases.english: Beit Shammai said to them: No,
if you said this regarding a menstruating woman
who, even if she immersed and saw blood, is impure,
will you say it regarding a woman who gave birth
who, if she immersed and saw blood, is pure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison brought in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between a נדה and a יולדת
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A נדה is stricter, because she is impure even after immersing, while a יולדת is pure after immersing.

steps.title: בית הלל prove their point from a יולדת בזוב
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל bring a case where immersing makes the difference: a יולדת בזוב is pure if she immersed, but impure if she did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to them: A woman who gave birth while a זבה will prove it. If she immersed and then saw blood after her seven counted days, she is pure. If she did not immerse and saw blood, she is impure!
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל answer בית שמאי's objection with a new case, which shows that not immersing really does keep a woman impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי said a יולדת is too lenient to compare to a נדה. בית הלל show that even for a יולדת, immersion is the key. In the case of a יולדת בזוב, the same blood is pure after immersion and impure without it. So a regular יולדת who did not immerse should also stay fully impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Will prove (a case brought as proof)
A woman who gave birth while she was a זבה
The seven clean days a זבה must count

steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל's key idea: for a יולדת, immersion is what moves her out of impurity. Without it, she is treated like a נדה.

phrases.english: They said to them: A woman who gave birth as a zava will prove it,
for if she immersed and saw blood
after the days of counting, she is pure,
if she did not immerse and saw blood, she is impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers בית שמאי's rejection in step 8 with a new proof from a different case.
steps.raayaObject: That a יולדת who did not immerse stays impure like a נדה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule for a יולדת בזוב: she is pure if she immersed, and impure if she did not

steps.title: בית שמאי say the same rule applies to the יולדת בזוב
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי reject בית הלל's proof. They hold that the יולדת בזוב case follows the same rule, so it cannot be used as a proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי said to them: the law is the same in that case too, and that is our answer to you.
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי push back on בית הלל's proof from step 9. They say the יולדת בזוב case has the same rule, so it proves nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל assumed everyone agrees that a יולדת בזוב who did not immerse is fully impure. בית שמאי deny this. They hold that even she, if she did not immerse, makes things impure only with wet blood. Since they do not accept the starting point, the proof falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: the law is the same (in that case too)
an answer or reply that pushes back on an argument
a woman who gave birth while she had the status of a זבה

steps.confusionAlert: בית שמאי are not giving in here. 'הוא הדין' means 'the same rule applies there too,' so they do not accept the case you brought as proof.

phrases.english: They said to them:
phrases.notes: Here 'they' is בית שמאי, answering בית הלל.

phrases.english: The law is the same, and that is the answer.
phrases.notes: They mean that a יולדת בזוב who did not immerse also makes things impure only while the blood is wet.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם: הוּא הַדִּין, וְהִיא הַתְּשׁוּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects בית הלל's proof from the יולדת בזוב case in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the יולדת בזוב case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: בית הלל assumed everyone agrees about that case. בית שמאי hold that the same lenient rule applies there.

steps.title: The משנה says בית שמאי agree about a יולדת בזוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges step 10. The משנה says בית שמאי agree that a יולדת בזוב makes things impure with wet or dry blood, so how can they argue here?
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean they argue about a יולדת בזוב? But the משנה teaches that בית שמאי agree that a יולדת בזוב makes things impure whether the blood is wet or dry!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sees a contradiction. In step 10 בית שמאי argue about the יולדת בזוב, but the משנה says they agree about her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 says בית שמאי are lenient with a יולדת בזוב: only wet blood makes things impure. The משנה says the opposite: בית שמאי agree her blood is impure wet or dry. Both statements cannot be true in the same case.

keyTerms.meaning: is this to say...? (opens a question about what follows from a statement)
they argue or disagree
they agree or concede
makes things impure whether the blood is wet or dry

phrases.english: Is this to say that they disagree?
But didn't we learn: And they agree regarding a woman who gave birth as a זבה
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה. 'They agree' means בית שמאי agree with בית הלל.

phrases.english: that she makes things impure, wet or dry!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges בית שמאי's position in step 10 using the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that בית שמאי argue about a יולדת בזוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says בית שמאי agree that a יולדת בזוב makes things impure wet or dry. This contradicts the claim that they are lenient with her.

steps.title: Counted versus did not count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the two sources speak about different women. They argue about a woman who counted her clean days and agree about a woman who did not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here they argue about a woman who counted her seven clean days. There, in the משנה, they agree about a woman who did not count them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by splitting the case into two situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the woman already counted her seven clean days but did not immerse, בית שמאי are lenient and say only wet blood makes things impure. If she has not counted yet, she is still fully a זבה, so even בית שמאי agree that wet or dry blood makes things impure. The משנה speaks of the second situation, and the argument is about the first.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not difficult (the question has an answer)
here... there (two different cases)
she counted her seven clean days

steps.whatToRemember: Counted but did not immerse: בית שמאי and בית הלל argue. Did not count at all: everyone agrees she makes things impure wet or dry.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
Here, where she counted,
phrases.notes: 'Counted' means she counted the seven clean days a זבה needs. The argument is about this case.

phrases.english: there, where she did not count.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא — כָּאן שֶׁסָּפְרָה, כָּאן שֶׁלֹּא סָפְרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources seemed to speak about the same יולדת בזוב, so they contradicted each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is about a woman who counted her clean days. The agreement in the משנה is about a woman who did not count.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the split
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that when a יולדת בזוב counted but did not immerse, each side follows its own view. This supports the answer in step 12.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so it is taught in a ברייתא: a woman who gave birth as a זבה, counted her clean days, did not immerse, and then saw blood: בית שמאי follow their view and בית הלל follow theirs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that confirms the answer in step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא describes exactly the 'counted but did not immerse' case. It says the two sides keep their usual views there: בית שמאי say only wet blood makes things impure, and בית הלל say wet or dry. This shows the argument really is about the woman who counted.

keyTerms.meaning: she immersed in a מקוה
she saw blood
according to their own view

phrases.english: And so it is taught: a woman who gave birth as a זבה, who counted
but did not immerse, and then saw blood,
בית שמאי follow their view,
and בית הלל follow their view.
phrases.notes: Their usual views: בית שמאי say only wet blood makes things impure, and בית הלל say wet or dry.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: יוֹלֶדֶת בְּזוֹב שֶׁסָּפְרָה וְלֹא טָבְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 12 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that the argument is about a woman who counted her clean days but did not immerse.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that describes this exact case and says each side keeps its own view.

steps.title: רב: one source, and the תורה decides its status
steps.stepSummary: רב holds that all of the יולדת's blood comes from one source. Whether it is pure or impure depends only on what the תורה says about that day.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב says there is one source. The תורה made its blood impure, and the תורה made its blood pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with רב's view: all the blood after childbirth comes from one source, and the תורה gives it its status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, the blood itself does not change. What changes is the day. On her impure days the תורה calls the blood impure, and on her pure days (דם טוהר) the תורה calls the same kind of blood pure.

keyTerms.meaning: A source or spring. Here it means the place in the body the blood comes from.
Pure blood. This is blood a woman sees during her days of purity after giving birth.
Made it impure / made it pure.

phrases.english: It was stated:
Rav says: It is one source —
the Torah made it impure
and the Torah made it pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: רַב אָמַר: מַעְיָן אֶחָד הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new אמוראים dispute about the blood of a יולדת. It does not continue the בית שמאי / בית הלל discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is one source. The status of the blood depends only on the day, as set by the תורה.

steps.title: לוי: two sources that take turns
steps.stepSummary: לוי holds that there are two separate sources, one for impure blood and one for pure blood. When one closes, the other opens.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי says there are two sources. When the impure one closes, the pure one opens. When the pure one closes, the impure one opens.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives לוי's opposing view: the pure blood and the impure blood come from two different sources.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For לוי, the status of the blood depends on which source it came from, not only on the calendar. The sources work in turns: at the end of her impure days the impure source shuts and the pure one opens, and at the end of her pure days the reverse happens.

keyTerms.meaning: Closes or is shut.
Opens.

steps.confusionAlert: Both רב and לוי agree on the schedule of impure and pure days. They argue only about where the blood physically comes from.

phrases.english: And Levi says: They are two sources —
the impure one closes, the pure one opens;
the pure one closes, the impure one opens.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing side of the dispute begun in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two sources that alternate. The blood's status depends on which source is open.

steps.title: What difference does it make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a practical case where רב and לוי would rule differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between רב and לוי. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the days decide everything, so both views seem to give the same results. The גמרא wants a case where the 'one source vs. two sources' question actually changes the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them? It asks for a case where the two opinions lead to different rulings.

phrases.english: What is between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the two views in steps 14 and 15 differ in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where רב and לוי would rule differently.

steps.title: The difference: blood that keeps flowing across the boundary
steps.stepSummary: The difference shows up when a woman has a steady flow of blood that starts on one side of a boundary day and continues past it.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them when a woman bleeds steadily from within the seven days into the time after seven, from within fourteen into after fourteen, from within forty into after forty, or from within eighty into after eighty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with four cases. In each one, a steady flow of blood keeps going across the line where impure days turn into pure days, or pure days turn back into regular days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After a boy she has 7 impure days and pure days until day 40. After a girl she has 14 impure days and pure days until day 80. If the blood never stops at the boundary, the question becomes whether the calendar decides its status (רב) or whether the source it started from still matters (לוי).

keyTerms.meaning: Bleeding in a steady, unbroken flow.
From within a time period into the time after it.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them:
one who flows steadily from within seven days into after seven,
phrases.notes: Seven is the number of impure days after a boy. After that her pure days begin.

phrases.aramaic: וּמִתּוֹךְ אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר לְאַחַר אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר,
phrases.english: and from within fourteen into after fourteen,
phrases.notes: Fourteen is the number of impure days after a girl.

phrases.english: and from within forty into after forty,
and from within eighty into after eighty.
phrases.notes: Forty and eighty are the days when her pure days end, for a boy and for a girl.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference appears when a steady flow continues past day 7 or 14 (into the pure days), or past day 40 or 80 (out of the pure days).

steps.title: How רב rules in these cases
steps.stepSummary: According to רב, the first cases end up lenient and the later cases end up strict.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רב, the first part is lenient and the last part is strict.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to explain how each view rules in the four cases, beginning with רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב only the day matters. Blood that flows from day 7 or 14 into the pure days becomes pure once the pure days start, so the ruling is lenient. Blood that flows past day 40 or 80 becomes impure once the pure days end, so the ruling is strict.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a list or teaching.
The last part of a list or teaching.
Toward leniency.
Toward strictness.

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רב's view follows directly from 'one source': the calendar alone decides. That sets up the contrast with לוי's view.

phrases.english: According to Rav — the first clause is to be lenient,
phrases.notes: The 'first clause' means the 7 and 14 cases, where the blood flows into her pure days.

phrases.english: and the latter clause is to be strict;
phrases.notes: The 'latter clause' means the 40 and 80 cases, where the blood flows past the end of her pure days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out how the cases of step 17 come out according to רב.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to רב, blood flowing into the pure days is pure (lenient), and blood flowing past the end of the pure days is impure (strict).

steps.title: לוי's ruling is the reverse of רב's
steps.stepSummary: According to לוי, in the first cases a continuous flow makes things strict, and in the later cases it makes things lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to לוי, the first cases are strict and the later cases are lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer about the practical difference. It shows that לוי rules the opposite way from רב in the same cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לוי says each kind of blood has its own source. So a flow that keeps going past a boundary day shows the blood is still coming from the same source it started from. In the first cases the flow begins in the impure days and runs into the pure days, so it stays impure (strict). In the later cases it begins in the pure days and runs past them, so it stays pure (lenient).

keyTerms.meaning: The first part or first cases
The last part or later cases
To be strict
To be lenient

steps.whatToRemember: רב: the day decides, so the first cases are lenient and the later cases are strict. לוי: a continuous flow keeps the status of the source it started from, so the first cases are strict and the later cases are lenient.

phrases.english: According to Levi — the first clause is stringent,
and the latter clause is lenient.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 18 by giving לוי's side.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In a continuous flow across a boundary day, לוי is strict in the first cases and lenient in the later cases.

steps.title: Quoting the dispute about a יולדת who did not immerse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: בית שמאי say the blood of an unimmersed יולדת is like saliva and urine, while בית הלל say it is impure whether moist or dry.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a משנה: the blood of a woman who gave birth and did not immerse. בית שמאי say it is like her saliva and her urine. בית הלל say it makes things impure whether moist or dry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה in order to challenge one of the two views. This step sets up the source, and the actual question comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saliva and urine of an impure woman only make things impure while they are still wet. Real נדה blood makes things impure even after it dries. בית הלל treat this blood like real נדה blood.

keyTerms.meaning: The blood of a woman who gave birth
She immersed in a מקוה
Like her saliva and her urine, which are impure only while moist
Moist and dry

phrases.english: They raised an objection: the blood of a woman who gave birth who did not immerse,
Beit Shammai say:
It is like her saliva and her urine,
and Beit Hillel say:
It imparts impurity whether moist or dry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge against the views laid out in steps 14 to 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: לוי's view that there are two separate sources
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sets up the משנה whose ruling by בית הלל will be shown to fit רב but not לוי.

steps.title: The משנה fits רב but seems to contradict לוי
steps.stepSummary: If the flow had stopped and new blood came in the pure days, בית הלל's strictness fits רב's one-source view. But under לוי, that blood comes from the pure source, so why is it impure?
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think the case is where the bleeding stopped. That works for רב, who says it is one source: that is why it makes things impure whether moist or dry. But for לוי, who says there are two sources, why should it make things impure whether moist or dry?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now states the challenge. It assumes the משנה's case is where her bleeding stopped and new blood came later, and asks how לוי can explain בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רב there is only one source, so the blood's status depends on her situation. Since she has not immersed, she is still treated as impure. Under לוי, new blood during the pure days should come from the pure source, so בית הלל's ruling that it is impure seems to make no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: It enters your mind; you might assume
The bleeding stopped
It makes sense for one view (setting up a contrast)
Source, spring

phrases.english: It enters your mind that her bleeding stopped.
Granted, according to Rav, who said:
It is one source,
for that reason it imparts impurity whether moist or dry.
But according to Levi, who said:
There are two sources,
why does it impart impurity whether moist or dry?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the quoted משנה into a direct challenge against לוי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the flow stopped, new blood in the pure days should come from the pure source under לוי. So בית הלל's ruling that it is fully impure contradicts him.

steps.title: לוי: the case is a continuous flow
steps.stepSummary: לוי answers that the משנה is talking about a woman whose bleeding never stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי can tell you: what case are we dealing with here? A woman with a continuous flow.
steps.whatsHappening: לוי defends himself by explaining the משנה's case differently. The flow did not stop.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the blood kept flowing from the impure days into the pure days, then under לוי it is still coming from the impure source. That is why בית הלל can call it fully impure. The challenge only worked because we assumed the bleeding had stopped.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (used to narrow a source to a specific case)
A woman who is flowing steadily without stopping

phrases.english: Levi could say to you:
Here, with what are we dealing?
With a woman who flows continuously,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ לֵוִי: הָכָא בְמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21 by redefining the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's case is where the bleeding stopped, so לוי cannot explain בית הלל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's case is a continuous flow, so under לוי the blood is from the impure source.

steps.title: Then why are בית שמאי lenient?
steps.stepSummary: If the flow is continuous and clearly from the impure source, how can בית שמאי treat it only like saliva and urine?
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is a continuous flow, what is the reason of בית שמאי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on לוי's answer. Now בית שמאי's lenient view seems hard to explain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we say the flow never stopped, the blood looks like plain impure blood. So why would בית שמאי say it is impure only while moist?

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: If it is with a woman who flows continuously,
what is the reason of Beit Shammai?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בְּשׁוֹפַעַת, מַאי טַעְמָא דְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 22 from the other side of the מחלוקת.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the משנה as a continuous flow
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In a continuous flow the blood is clearly impure, so בית שמאי's leniency seems to have no reason.

steps.title: בית שמאי hold like רב: one source
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי hold there is only one source, so blood in the pure days is pure even if the flow is continuous.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי hold that it is one source.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that בית שמאי simply hold like רב's view, that it is all one source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the one-source view, the day decides, not where the flow started. So for בית שמאי, blood in the pure days is not full נדה blood. בית הלל hold like לוי, and the משנה is no longer a problem for לוי.

keyTerms.meaning: They hold, they are of the opinion
One single source for pure and impure blood

steps.whatToRemember: לוי reads the משנה as a continuous flow. בית הלל then fit his two-source view, and בית שמאי hold the one-source view like רב.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai hold:
It is one source.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבְרִי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי: מַעְיָן אֶחָד הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 23 by tying בית שמאי to רב's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing different underlying views to the disputing sides
steps.terutzHavaAmina: In a continuous flow, everyone should agree the blood is fully impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית שמאי hold there is one source, so the day decides. Their argument with בית הלל is the same as the argument between רב and לוי.

steps.title: Under רב, what are בית שמאי and בית הלל arguing about?
steps.stepSummary: Under לוי, the dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל is clear: one source or two. Under רב, who says there is only one source, what is left for them to argue about?
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to לוי, that explains the difference between בית שמאי and בית הלל. But according to רב, what is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to challenge רב. It asks what בית שמאי and בית הלל could be arguing about if רב is right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 24 the dispute was explained as one source (בית שמאי) against two sources (בית הלל), and that fits לוי. But רב holds that everyone agrees there is just one source. So under רב that explanation is gone, and the גמרא needs some other point the two houses disagree on.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted; this works fine (for one view), but...
What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: Granted, according to Levi,

phrases.aramaic: הַיְינוּ דְּאִיכָּא בֵּין בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל,
phrases.english: that is how there is a difference between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel,
but according to Rav, what is the difference between them?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְלֵוִי הַיְינוּ דְּאִיכָּא בֵּין בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל אֶלָּא לְרַב מַאי בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer in step 24 (one source vs. two) to show that רב cannot explain the dispute the same way.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that pure and impure blood come from one source.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If everyone agrees there is one source, the one-source vs. two-source explanation of the dispute disappears, and the dispute seems to have no basis.

steps.title: They argue about days alone versus days plus immersion
steps.stepSummary: Under רב, the two houses argue about what makes the blood pure. בית שמאי say the days alone do it. בית הלל say it takes the days and immersion.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is days and immersion. בית שמאי hold that the תורה made it depend on the days. בית הלל hold that it depends on the days and immersion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רב a new point of dispute. The two houses argue about whether her blood becomes pure just because the days have passed, or only after she also immerses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בית שמאי, once her pure days begin her blood is pure even without immersion. It is only like her saliva and urine, which are impure when moist. For בית הלל, without immersion the blood is still real impure blood, so it makes impure whether moist or dry. This way רב keeps one source and still explains the dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: The days (the set count of days after birth)
Immersion in a מקוה
The תורה made it depend on...

steps.whatToRemember: Under רב: בית שמאי say the days alone make the blood pure; בית הלל say it takes days plus טבילה.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them: days and immersion,
for Beit Shammai hold:
the Merciful One made it depend on the days,
and Beit Hillel hold: on the days and immersion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25 by giving a different basis for the dispute under רב.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different point of dispute that has nothing to do with the number of sources.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Under רב the two houses would have nothing to argue about.
steps.terutzMaskana: They argue whether the blood's purity depends on the days alone or on the days and טבילה.

steps.title: The next line of the משנה: a woman who gave birth while a זבה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: everyone agrees that a woman who gave birth while she was a זבה makes impure whether the blood is moist or dry. It assumes this too is a case where her flow stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: and they agree that a woman who gives birth while a זבה makes impure whether moist or dry. You would think that here too, it is a case where the flow stopped.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the next line of the משנה and assumes what case it describes. This sets up a challenge that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even בית שמאי agree that when she gave birth as a זבה, her blood makes impure moist or dry. Just as it did with the earlier line of the משנה in step 21, the גמרא first assumes the case is where her bleeding stopped and new blood came later. That assumption is what creates the problem in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who gives birth while she is a זבה
They agree (here, בית שמאי agree with בית הלל)
You might think; it enters your mind
(Her flow) stopped

phrases.english: Come and hear: and they agree about a woman who gives birth while a zavah,
that she makes impure whether moist or dry.
You would think that here too it is where her flow stopped.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה's dispute to its next clause, to test רב and לוי again.
steps.raayaObject: Whether רב or לוי fits the משנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's clause that everyone agrees a יולדת בזוב makes impure moist or dry, read as a case where the flow stopped.
steps.kashyaTarget: לוי's view that there are two separate sources
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sets up the משנה's clause about a יולדת בזוב. Read as a case where her flow stopped, it will fit רב but not לוי.

steps.title: This line fits רב but seems to contradict לוי
steps.stepSummary: Under רב, one source, so the blood is still זבה blood and makes impure moist or dry. Under לוי, new blood in the pure days comes from the pure source. So why would it make impure moist or dry?
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted according to רב, who said it is one source: that is why it makes impure moist or dry. But according to לוי, who said there are two sources, why does it make impure moist or dry?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the משנה's line to challenge לוי. It shows that the line fits רב easily but seems wrong under לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רב there is one source, and she is still a זבה whom the תורה has not yet made pure, so her blood is fully impure. Under לוי, once the flow stopped, new blood in the pure days comes from the pure source. At most it should be like a זבה's saliva or urine, which is impure only when moist.

keyTerms.meaning: One source (of blood)
Two sources (a pure one and an impure one)
Why?

steps.confusionAlert: Saliva and urine of a זבה are impure only while moist. Her actual impure blood makes impure even when dry. The whole question is which group this blood belongs to.

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַב, דְּאָמַר: מַעְיָן אֶחָד הוּא,
phrases.english: Granted according to Rav, who said: it is one source,
that is why it makes impure moist or dry.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְלֵוִי, דְּאָמַר: שְׁנֵי מַעְיָנוֹת הֵן,
phrases.english: But according to Levi, who said: there are two sources,
why does it make impure moist or dry?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַב דְּאָמַר מַעְיָן אֶחָד הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the case assumed in step 27 (the flow stopped) and shows it fits רב but contradicts לוי.
steps.kashyaTarget: לוי's view that there are two separate sources.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the flow stopped, under לוי new blood in the pure days comes from the pure source. So it should not make impure when dry, yet the משנה says it does.

steps.title: לוי says the משנה is about a continuous flow
steps.stepSummary: לוי answers that the משנה about a woman who gave birth as a זבה is talking about a woman whose bleeding never stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי could say to you: here too, the case is one where she kept bleeding without a break.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 28 for לוי. It says the משנה is not about a woman whose flow stopped, but about one whose bleeding kept going.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 27 the גמרא assumed the flow had stopped, which made the משנה hard for לוי. If the bleeding ran straight from the impure days into the pure days, then this blood is still coming from the impure source. So even לוי agrees it makes impure, whether moist or dry.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman whose bleeding keeps flowing without stopping
Here too, meaning the same answer used earlier works here as well

phrases.english: He could say to you:
phrases.notes: "He" is לוי, the one who holds there are two sources.

phrases.english: Here too, it is a case of a continuous flow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28 against לוי by changing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is about a woman whose flow stopped, so the blood should come from the pure source according to לוי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a continuous flow, so the blood comes from the impure source even according to לוי.

steps.title: Why would the משנה need to teach something so obvious?
steps.stepSummary: If her bleeding never stopped, it is obvious the blood is impure, so why would the משנה bother to say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If she kept bleeding, why did the משנה need to teach this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on לוי's answer. If the case is a continuous flow, the rule seems too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה is not supposed to teach something everyone already knows. Blood that keeps flowing from the impure days is clearly impure blood. So this answer seems to make the משנה's statement pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: Why was it needed? The question of why a source would teach something obvious

phrases.english: If it is a case of a continuous flow,
why was it needed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: לוי's explanation that the משנה is about a continuous flow.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the flow is continuous, the impurity is obvious, so the משנה would be teaching nothing new.

steps.title: The משנה is needed to limit בית שמאי's rule
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that בית שמאי's rule, that the days alone make the blood pure, works only for a plain birth and not for a woman who gave birth as a זבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed for בית שמאי. Even though בית שמאי say it is one source and the תורה made it depend on the days, that is only for a woman who simply gave birth, whose days are finished. But a woman who gave birth as a זבה, who needs to count clean days, is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why the משנה had to teach this. It is not obvious according to בית שמאי, so the משנה teaches a limit on their view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי say there is one source, and once her days are over the blood is pure even if it keeps flowing (step 24). So one might think a continuous flow is pure for them here too. The משנה teaches that a woman who gave birth as a זבה still needs to count seven clean days, so her days are not yet complete and the blood stays impure, moist or dry.

keyTerms.meaning: One source: the view that pure and impure blood come from the same place
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
A woman who simply gave birth, with no זיבה
A woman who gave birth while she was a זבה
Counting, here the counting of seven clean days

steps.whatToRemember: According to בית שמאי, the days alone make the blood pure, but only once her days are truly complete. A woman who gave birth as a זבה still has to count seven clean days first.

phrases.english: It was needed for בית שמאי.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּקָאָמְרִי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי:
phrases.english: Even though בית שמאי say:
It is one source,
and the Torah made it depend on the days,
that applies only to a woman who simply gave birth,
whose days have been completed.
But a woman who gave birth as a זבה,
who needs counting, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30 by showing what the משנה adds.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a new point the source teaches (חידוש)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: According to בית שמאי, any blood after her days is pure, even a continuous flow from a woman who gave birth as a זבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A woman who gave birth as a זבה needs counting, so her days are not complete and the blood stays impure even for בית שמאי.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the three things included by דְּוֹתָהּ תִּטְמָא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that learns three things from the words דְּוֹתָהּ תִּטְמָא, including that a woman who gave birth as a זבה must count seven clean days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: "Her menstrual sickness she shall be impure" includes the man who has relations with her. It includes the nights. And it includes a woman who gave birth as a זבה, teaching that she must count seven clean days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to test רב and לוי. This step only quotes the ברייתא; the next step starts using it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the same words from the פסוק three times. The key part is the third: a woman who gave birth as a זבה must count seven clean days. The גמרא will ask which view, רב or לוי, can explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: Her menstrual sickness she shall be impure (ויקרא 12:2)
To include, meaning to add another case to the law
The man who has relations with her
Seven clean days, with no bleeding, that a זבה must count

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"Her menstrual sickness she shall be impure":
to include the man who has relations with her.
"Her menstrual sickness she shall be impure":
to include the nights.
"Her menstrual sickness she shall be impure":
to include a woman who gave birth as a זבה,
that she must count seven clean days.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: ״דְּוֹתָהּ תִּטְמָא״ — לְרַבּוֹת אֶת בּוֹעֲלָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the משנה is settled, brings a new source to test the two views.
steps.raayaObject: The dispute between רב (one source) and לוי (two sources).
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading דְּוֹתָהּ תִּטְמָא (ויקרא 12:2) to require seven clean days for a woman who gave birth as a זבה.

steps.title: The ברייתא fits רב, who says there is one source
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא makes sense according to רב: since there is one source, her זבה blood continues, so she needs seven clean days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to רב, who said it is one source, that is why she needs seven clean days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its challenge with "granted." It shows the ברייתא fits רב, setting up the question that will come against לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב there is only one source, so the blood of the pure days is still the same זבה blood. That is why she must stop bleeding and count seven clean days. The open question, coming next, is how לוי explains this if blood in the pure days comes from a pure source.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted: the first half of a challenge, saying the source fits one view before asking about the other

steps.confusionAlert: This step is not the full challenge. The "granted" only says the ברייתא fits רב; the hard part, against לוי, comes in the next lines.

phrases.english: Granted, according to רב,
who said it is one source,

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם הָכִי בָּעֲיָא שִׁבְעָה יָמִים נְקִיִּים,
phrases.english: that is why she needs seven clean days.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַב דְּאָמַר מַעְיָן אֶחָד הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts analyzing the ברייתא of step 32, beginning with רב's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: לוי, who holds there are two sources (the challenge will be finished in the next lines).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The need for seven clean days makes sense if the blood is still זבה blood, as רב says. According to לוי, blood in the pure days comes from a pure source, so why should she need to count?
